left:
Rafael Nuifez and colleagues studied how members of the Yupno, an Indigenous group in
Papua New Guinea, conceptualize time in both spoken language and gestures. The
researchers recorded Yupno speakers explaining certain temporal words and phrases,
such as jare, a past-oriented expression that translates to “day before yesterday,” and coded
each speaker’s manual gestures. Previous research has found a tendency in many cultures
to make temporal distinctions along imagined linear axes: for instance, Hebrew speakers
often refer to the right/left axis to describe events in time. Some researchers believe this
tendency is universal, but Nunez and colleagues claim this is not the case.
